433: Something is wrong with this cluster's data. The top-weighted defining datasheet is the Defiler — a Chaos Space Marines Daemon Engine with no place in any Adeptus Custodes list — and the playstyle axes scatter across six different archetypes without a dominant signal, which is the fingerprint of a noise cluster rather than a coherent tournament archetype. With only 14 games played across 7 lists, there is not enough data to establish a reliable identity. Do not use this description for competitive reference; flag the cluster for manual review and re-clustering before publishing.
459: Built around Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, a Rogal Dorn Commander, and a Baneblade anchor, this is a Recon Element-flavored Grizzled Company hybrid that leans heavily into mobile firepower rather than a static Russ castle. The engine is using Scout Sentinel infiltrate-and-screen to deny deep-strike approach lanes while the Baneblade and Rogal Dorn pump high-AP, Blast-template fire into mid-board, scoring primary through sheer OC weight backed by infantry and vehicle bulk. Against slow Transport Infantry and Mass Volume Horde lists, the combination of Hellhound flame templates (auto-hit, ignore cover) and Russ Blast weapons deletes screening bodies efficiently before they can contest. However, mobile skimmer and melee-toolbox lists crack this build open badly — Scout Sentinels are T5 with a 4+ save and fold instantly to anti-armour fire, and once the Baneblade is isolated by fast flanking units, the list loses its damage anchor without the activation count to recover on primary.
434: Built around wall-to-wall Custodian Guard and Wardens backed by Trajann Valoris and a Blade Champion, this is Shield Host running a dense elite infantry brawler with every model punching above its weight class. It scores by planting 2+/4++ bodies on midfield objectives turn one and refusing to move — Trajann's re-roll aura and the Blade Champion's Martial Ka'tahs keep the damage output high enough that clearing a single contested point costs the opponent more than it's worth. Stacked 2+/4++ across T5-6 chassis laughs at anything relying on AP-1 or AP-2 chip removal, making it a nightmare for mid-tier combat brawlers and transport-infantry lists trying to trade into elite bodies. It cracks open when concentrated AP-3+ Melta or Demolisher cannon fire forces wound rolls that bypass the save stack entirely, and fast skimmer or mobile anti-armour lists that can dictate range keep the Custodian bricks permanently out of their preferred engagement distance.
498: Built around Celestian Sacresants and Arco-Flagellants delivered into melee under cover of Ministorum Priest buffs, Repentia squads, and the Triumph of Saint Katherine's miracle-dice engine, this is a Hallowed Martyrs-flavored beatdown list that floods mid-board with bodies rather than vehicles. It wins by generating Miracle Dice through the Triumph and Sanctifiers, spending them to guarantee critical wound rolls on Repentia chain-swords and Arco-Flagellant electroflails, then sticking objectives with high-OC screens of Celestian Insidiants that opponents struggle to shove off. The wide model count and multiple invuln-stacked melee units punish slow grind lists and anything that can't clear bodies efficiently — Transport Infantry shells and static gunlines concede primary turn after turn once the screen locks in. Fast kiting armies and massed Melta, however, crack it open: Drukhari Raiders out-tempo the advance, and concentrated AP-3+ volume removes the melee hammers before they ever reach charge range.
453: Built around Warp Spiders, Corsair Voidreavers, Rangers, Fire Dragons, Howling Banshees, and Warlock Skyrunners, this is an Aspect Host shell that layers Pistol/Assault skimmer mobility on top of Preternatural Precision's Lethal Hits stack, producing a list that simultaneously kites and spikes. The engine scores by using Voidreaver and Ranger chaff to contest objectives while Warp Spiders teleport into isolated targets and Fire Dragons drop Melta at point-blank, with Banshees closing under Banshee Mask 4+ invuln to trigger the melee Lethal Hits chain via Shrine Tokens. It punishes static Heavy Gunline and slow durable-grind lists that can't match the 12"+ repositioning tempo, letting Warp Spider jump-shooters and Wave Serpent-delivered Dragons dictate which target burns each turn. The 44.9% win rate signals it struggles where its two axes collide — anti-vehicle mobile lists like Mont'ka or Infernal Lance match its speed AND crack the fragile aspect chassis with AP-3+ Melta before the invuln stacks matter.
493: Built around Vertus Praetors and a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike as the primary strike vector, with Allarus Custodians and a Telemon providing anvil weight and Witchseekers screening the flanks, this is a jetbike-cavalry list that plays closer to a Rhino-rush mech shell than a traditional Custodes gunline — the high transportInfantry and midTBrawler scores reflect how it uses speed as delivery rather than kite. The plan is to flood mid-board objectives on turn 1 with 2+/4++ jetbike bodies that are almost impossible to shift per-point, then score primary while Allarus deep strike threatens to punish any counter-commitment. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count anti-armour lists that can't generate the volume of AP-3+ Melta shots needed to crack T6 2+/4++ models efficiently across multiple activations. It cracks open against layered Lethal Hits builds and heavy indirect fire — Plagueburst Crawlers and Avenger Gatling Cannons can eventually overload even a 4++ when the wound volume is high enough and the jetbikes have nowhere to reposition.
499: Built around Castigators, Zephyrim, Dominions, and Exorcists backed by Immolators and a jump-pack Canoness, this is a Bringers of Flame list running a hybrid gunline-skirmish shell rather than a pure burn focus. The plan is to park Castigators and Exorcists in a fire-base that forces the opponent to advance into Dominion flamer range, while Zephyrim and the Canoness deliver jump-infantry pressure from deep strike to deny objective contest and draw fire off the vehicles. It punishes slow midfield-grind armies — Transport Infantry Rhino-rushes and Mass Volume Horde blobs that walk into Castigator Blast templates and Exorcist S8 AP-3 missile salvos at 48" — by never needing to close the distance. Against fast mobile lists that match its threat range, especially Mobile Anti-Armour vehicles or skimmer kite armies that can strip Immolators and Castigators before the fire-base establishes, the list's modest invuln profile and a win rate well below 50% reveal how hard it struggles to protect its own shooting platform.
440: Built around Sicarian Ruststalkers and Infiltrators moving up with Pteraxii Skystalkers and Ironstrider Ballistarii in the Skitarii Hunter Cohort, this is an aggressive mid-board pressure list that tries to deliver multiple melee and harassment threats simultaneously across a wide frontage. The engine is Ruststalker and Infiltrator units closing into combat range under Skystalker screening, with Ironstrider Ballistarii providing mobile AP-2 support fire while Rangers and the Skitarii Marshal anchor secondary scoring. It punishes slow, planted lists — particularly infantry blobs and heavy-gunline builds that can't reposition to face threats arriving from multiple angles — through activation-count pressure and the sheer variety of threat vectors a wide Skitarii roster presents. What cracks it open is concentrated anti-infantry firepower at range: with no meaningful invulnerable saves, no Feel No Pain, and T3 across almost the entire roster, anything that efficiently clears models before the Sicarians close — War Horde Sustained Hits 1, Russ blast templates, Pactbound crit-stacking — collapses the delivery mechanism before it can engage.
494: Built around Contemptor-Achillus, Contemptor-Galatus, and Telemon Heavy Dreadnoughts anchored by Caladius Grav-Tanks and Witchseeker screens, this Solar Spearhead list floods the board with T8-10 walker chassis carrying 4+ invulnerable saves and exceptional melee punch. The plan is to march Dreadnoughts into midfield objectives turn 2, using Witchseekers as a forward screen and the Caladius to threaten anything the walkers can't reach — grinding primary scoring through sheer durability rather than a single damage spike. The multi-Dreadnought chassis stack punishes static gunlines and mid-T brawlers that can't efficiently clear T8+ targets with AP-2 or better, forcing opponents to commit entire damage budgets to a single walker while the rest score freely. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta fire or mass mobile anti-armour pressure cracks it open — with no transport delivery and moderate base movement, the castle can be isolated and dismantled chassis-by-chassis before it reaches engagement range.
497: Built around Celestian Sacresants and a Hospitaller keeping them alive, with Seraphim providing fast flanking pressure and Castigators delivering the long-range anti-armour punch, this is Hallowed Martyrs doing what it was designed to do. The plan is to park Sacresants on mid-board objectives behind a Sisters Novitiate screen, let the Hospitaller's healing engine sustain them through the attrition game, and use Seraphim to contest flanks and deny secondaries while Castigators crack anything the melee can't reach. It punishes slower shooty lists — anything without the speed or AP volume to remove a 4+ invuln melee brick before it locks objectives finds itself perpetually behind on primary. The weakness is concentrated anti-infantry firepower at range: blast-heavy lists that can clear the Novitiate screen and strand the Sacresants without a target to charge before the Hospitaller's healing matters leave this list scoring into nothing.
492:
Built around Custodian Guard and Custodian Wardens as the scoring core, with Blade Champion, Venatari, and Allarus as the strike package and a Caladius providing vehicle fire support, this is a Talons of the Emperor list that plays like transport infantry minus the transports — dense elite bodies pushed forward into midfield on foot, backed by a Caladius threat.

The engine is objective saturation through high-OC elite infantry: Custodian Guard hold the center while Venatari deepstrike onto contested markers and Allarus Terminators teleport in to assassinate characters or crack isolated units, accumulating primary while the opponent can't efficiently clear 2+/4++ bodies per turn.

It punishes mid-table brawler lists hardest — Ork War Horde and Da Big Hunt can throw sixty attacks into a Custodian Guard squad and bounce off 2+/4++ saves, while the Blade Champion and Allarus counter-punch for far more efficient wounds in return.

Fast anti-armour threats crack it open: concentrated AP-3+ Melta or Knight-scale Avenger Gatling fire that cares nothing for 4++ invulns on T5 chassis will grind the limited model count down faster than the scoring engine can compensate, since there is no transport shell to replace lost models or absorb the alpha.
438: Built around Kastelan Robots with Cybernetica Datasmith direction, Onager Dunecrawlers, and Skorpius Disintegrators as the fire-support backbone, this is the Haloscreed Battle Clade expression of AdMech — a slow, durable armored column with Belisarius Cawl anchoring the character stack. The plan is to plant Kastelans in a defended midfield position where their Phosphor Blasters and Kastelan Fists generate oppressive volume — Cawl's reroll aura plus Dunecrawler Neutron Laser and Disintegrator fire strips the field of anything that tries to contest, while Rangers hold home objectives. It punishes static gunlines and mid-board brawlers badly: T6 Robots with 3+/5++ and Datasmith repair absorb anti-infantry firepower that can't efficiently crack the wound pool, and the Dunecrawler's Cognis Heavy Stubber + Neutron Laser profile covers both horde-clear and anti-armor in the same chassis. The weakness is speed — any mobile threat that deepstrikes into the Kastelan bubble or kites the firing arcs forces the list to react without the movement tools to answer, and concentrated AP-3 Melta at close range bypasses the invuln stack faster than Datasmith repairs can keep up.
439: Built around Hastarii Fusiliers delivered in Skorpius Duneriders, buffed by a Tech-Priest Manipulus and directed by a Skitarii Marshal, this is an aggressive mechanized Skitarii gunline that plays nothing like its name suggests — it's a Rhino-rush list in AdMech clothing, pushing transports forward and disgorging high-volume S5/AP-1 Hastarii fire at close range. The engine is the Manipulus's Optimised Cortex buff extending Hastarii Rapid Fire range to 30", letting squads shoot at full volume from inside or beside a Dunerider while Kataphron Destroyers and Servitor Battleclades anchor the midfield and punish anything that contests. It absolutely shreds mid-toughness elite infantry and transport-heavy lists that cluster in the midfield — the combination of massed Rapid Fire volume, Sustained Hits from the Marshal's order, and Kataphron plasma covering anything T5-7 means MEQ and comparable targets melt before they can trade back. What cracks it open is dedicated anti-tank focus: the Duneriders are T6 with a 3+ save and no invuln, so a single round of concentrated AP-3+ Melta or Lascannon fire strands expensive Fusilier squads on foot, collapsing the delivery engine before the gunline gets to dictate range.
454:
Built around Wraithguard, Wraithblades, and Wraithlords buffed by Spiritseers and Eldrad Ulthran, Spirit Conclave is the Aeldari wraith-construct brick — T6-7 models with 4+ invulnerable saves stacked via Protect/Jinx psychic actions and Shrine Token buffs, delivering Lethal Hits through Preternatural Precision on D-scythes and wraithcannons that auto-wound on 2s.

The plan is to advance the wraith wall onto midfield objectives by turn 2, hold them with sticky scoring, and use Eldrad's Psychic Fortress plus Fortune to make the brick functionally unkillable while D-scythe fire and Wraithblade melee grind through the opponent's scoring units.

The 4+/5+ invuln stack absorbs the kind of concentrated MEQ or elite-infantry firepower that dismantles most Aeldari lists, and T7 Wraithlords shrug off AP-1 and AP-2 chip shooting that skimmer lists rely on to trade efficiently.

Mobile Anti-Armour lists — Knights and Mont'ka Battlesuits with sustained Melta at AP-3 and Damage 6+ — crack T6-7 cleanly through the invuln, and the Spirit Conclave's 6" move and zero kite-potential means it cannot escape concentrated firepower, leaving a 31% win rate that reflects how badly the
458: Built around Kasrkin, Cadian Shock Troops, Tempestus Scions, and Attilan Rough Riders delivered in Chimeras, this is a Bridgehead Strike list caught between two identities — elite mech infantry trying to function as both a planted gunline and a volume-scoring horde simultaneously. It scores by flooding objectives with high-OC Cadian blobs and Chimera-borne Kasrkin, using the Militarum Tempestus Command Squad to layer orders onto Scion deep-strikers for a mid-game secondary-objective spike. The multi-axis pressure is theoretically punishing against lists that can't answer both massed S3-4 shooting and Rough Rider charge threats, but in practice no single phase is developed enough to close games efficiently. The same split focus that gives it flexibility is what kills it — without the Russ blast-template backbone of true Grizzled Company, it can't clear hordes, and without enough fast chassis it loses the primary race to any dedicated Mobile Toolbox or Transport Infantry list that commits to a single lane.
475: Built around Sword Brethren and Assault Intercessors led by a Marshal and Castellan, this Righteous Crusaders list pairs a Repulsor Executioner fire base with aggressive melee infantry to create a hybrid threat the opponent must answer on two axes simultaneously. The engine scores by pushing Sword Brethren and Assault Intercessors forward onto midfield objectives under cover of Repulsor Executioner main-gun fire — the Executioner's Macro Plasma Incinerator and Heavy Onslaught Cannon handle the anti-elite and anti-vehicle work while the melee infantry contest primary, with Scout Squads screen-clearing and locking secondaries. It punishes static gunlines that can't reposition, as the Repulsor's 24"+ threat range combined with charging Sword Brethren forces the opponent to split attention between surviving shooting and stopping the melee delivery. It cracks open against fast skimmer or mobile anti-armour lists — anything with 12"+ movement and AP-3 or better strips the Repulsor at range before the melee infantry can close, collapsing the scoring engine before it gets started.
446: Built around Assault Intercessors on foot and with jump packs backed by Gladiator Lancers, Ballistus Dreadnoughts, and a Baal Predator, this is a Liberator Assault Group–style midfield-rush list that leans harder into fire support than the typical Sons of Sanguinius melee hammer. The plan is to flood midfield with high-OC jump infantry using Scout Squads as cheap forward screens, then let the Lancer and Ballistus pick off key targets while the Assault Intercessors contest and score. It punishes slow-moving armies that can't clear bodies efficiently — the volume of mid-T infantry soaks fire while the vehicle trio deletes exposed characters and elite anchor units. Against faster, fragile skimmer lists or concentrated anti-armour, the hybrid identity collapses: the vehicles are too light to trade with Knights or Mont'ka Battlesuits, and the infantry screen folds before dedicated blast templates or fire-and-fade AP-2 volume.
460: Built around Death Korps of Krieg infantry blobs, Leman Russ Vanquishers, Death Riders, and Artillery Teams, this is a Grizzled Company-adjacent Krieg castle — dense bodies holding ground while long-range anti-armour and indirect fire do the killing work. It tries to win by planting 30-40 Krieg infantry on primary objectives turn one, using Vanquisher Cannons (S14 AP-3) and Artillery Teams to systematically delete high-value targets at range while Death Riders deliver Krieg Command Squad buffs to contested flanks. It punishes Transport Infantry lists that need to close distance — Rhinos and Land Raiders get cracked by Vanquisher fire before they unload, and the infantry blob absorbs whatever survives. Unfortunately, the activation count still can't match a true Mass Volume Horde on objectives, and any mobile list that outflanks the static firing line — particularly skimmer kite armies or deepstrike threats — exposes how little this force can reposition once committed.
444: Built around Vindicators as the armoured centrepiece, Sanguinary Guard as the elite melee hammer, and Incursors plus Inceptors providing board coverage, this is a Liberator Assault Group list that blends siege firepower with jump-pack aggression. The Vindicator's S14 AP-3 Demolisher Siege Cannon does the heavy lifting against elite infantry and light vehicles, while the Captain with Jump Pack and Sanguinary Guard deliver the close-range killing blow once the gun strips a unit's saves. It punishes mid-density MEQ and elite infantry lists that lack the invulnerable saves to weather AP-3 blast templates followed by a Sanguinary Guard charge, and Incursors with Inceptor overwatch cover denies easy counter-charges. However, at 41% win rate this build struggles against faster kiting lists and volume-horde armies — the Vindicator's 12" move and 24" range means skimmer-fire lists can deny firing arcs, while mass-infantry hordes absorb the blast damage through sheer wound count and out-score on objectives before the jump-pack hammer arrives.
476: Built around Crusader Squads in bulk, a Crusade Ancient banner-bearer, the Execrator daemon-hunting dreadnought, and Bladeguard Veterans as the elite hammer, this is Righteous Crusaders running a high-body melee-infantry castle with genuine fire support ambitions. The plan is to flood midfield objectives with large Crusader blobs backed by the Ancient's Ld-and-reroll aura, use the Execrator's multi-profile threat to deter or punish aggressive vehicle plays, and outscore on primary through sheer OC volume while Infiltrators deny deep-strike lanes into the backfield. It punishes slow gunlines and positional armies that can't clear a buffed 10-model Crusader squad per turn — the Ancient's banner plus Lieutenant reroll stacking makes these blobs obnoxiously sticky on objectives. However, the mixed axis signature (simultaneously trying to be a horde, a gunline, and a mech list) betrays a lack of single-minded identity, and any fast mobile anti-armour or skimmer list that ignores the blob and farms secondaries will expose how slowly this list converts OC into scored points.
447: Built around Chosen as the primary hammer unit delivered via Chaos Rhinos, with Raptors and Warp Talons providing fast-moving flanking threats and Huron Blackheart anchoring the force inside the Huron's Marauders detachment. The engine is a Rhino-rush delivery plan combined with aggressive aerial harassment — Chosen disembark onto contested objectives while Raptors and Warp Talons exploit gaps in the opponent's screen, scoring primary through sustained multi-vector pressure rather than a single spike. The multi-axis threat profile punishes opponents who can only answer one direction at once, particularly static gunlines and transport-light lists that can't reposition to cover both the ground push and the deep-striking flankers simultaneously. At sub-50% win rate, the build struggles against opponents who can outshoot the Rhinos before the Chosen disembark — Heavy Gunline lists with Blast weapons pop the transports on turn 1 and strand the hammers in the open, collapsing the delivery engine before it fires.
445: Built around Lemartes leading Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Death Company Dreadnoughts, and Sanguinary Guard in what reads as a Liberator Assault Group shell, this is a pure jump-pack melee hammer with zero ranged threat and maximum orbital commitment. The engine is Lemartes's aura stacking with Astorath and a Chaplain With Jump Pack to push Death Company into Devastating Wounds and extra-attack territory, then crashing the whole package onto a priority target and grinding outward from that initial trade. Against slow positional lists — Mass Volume Horde blobs, Heavy Gunline Russes — the 12" jump move plus Heroic Intervention stacking lets the list dictate where fights happen and clear objectives faster than the opponent can replace bodies. The build suffers badly against anything that out-ranges or outpaces it: a kiting Skimmer Skirmish list stays at 24"+ and chips the fragile 3+/no-invuln Death Company models off until the punch is gone, and without transport delivery the list is devastatingly exposed to screens that absorb the charge and deny the Lethal Hits spike on the turns it matters most.
463: Built around Bloodcrushers, Bloodletters, and Flesh Hounds delivered by a Rendmaster on Blood Throne and Skullmaster, with a Bloodthirster anchoring the hammer, this is Blood Legion doing what Khorne Daemons do best — stacking melee threat density across every tier of the roster. The engine is speed-and-charge: Flesh Hounds screen and threaten turn-1 engagements, Bloodcrushers (T5, 4+ invuln) absorb the counter-punch while Bloodletters pile in behind, and the Rendmaster's aura stacks Lethal Hits onto the charge to bypass high-toughness targets without relying on AP. It punishes Mid-T Brawler and Mass Volume Horde lists hardest — Lethal Hits on S5 Bloodcrusher weapons sidesteps the toughness wall on T5-6 mobs, and the 4+ invuln stack absorbs the counter-charge that would otherwise clear the wave. Mobile Anti-Armour and Transport Infantry crack it open: Knights concentrate AP-3+ Melta onto the Bloodthirster before the charge connects, while Rhino-rush lists use Cultist screens to absorb the first wave and crit-shoot the Rendmaster off the table before the Lethal Hits engine fires.
461: Built around Rotigus, a Great Unclean One, and dense blocks of Plaguebearers screened by Nurglings and Beasts of Nurgle, this is a Plague Legion wall — every unit drips with overlapping defensive layers and the whole army fights like a slow-moving infection. The win condition is planting Plaguebearers on objectives with sticky-scoring support, using Beasts of Nurgle as tarpit shock-absorbers to deny counter-charges, while Rotigus and the Great Unclean One grind forward with Lethal Hits weapon profiles and Disgustingly Resilient-equivalent FNP stacked on T6-7 bodies behind 5+ invulns. It punishes Mid-T Brawler and Mass Volume Horde lists brutally — Lethal Hits sidesteps toughness math, the Nurgling screen eats activation slots, and a 30-model Plaguebearer blob simply cannot be cleared off an objective in one shooting phase by anything without Blast or AP-2+. Mobile Anti-Armour with concentrated Melta and AP-3+ cracks it open, since neither Plaguebearers nor Greater Daemons carry the movement or invuln depth to survive focused Knight-equivalent firepower before the scoring gap becomes irreversible.
470: Built around a full pack of Wardogs — Brigands, Karnivores, Stalkers, and Executioners supported by a Cultist Mob screen — this is Houndpack Lance at its most committed, flooding the board with eight-plus T8 chassis at 12" move before the opponent can establish firing lanes. The engine is speed plus volume: Brigands bring indirect-fire arc denial while Karnivores close to melta range and Executioners stack AP-3+ autocannon volume, letting the pack concentrate on isolated targets turn by turn while Cultists hold home objectives. It punishes low-activation gunlines like Grizzled Company hardest, where the Wardog activation advantage overwhelms the Russ order economy before the tank company can clear enough hull points. The critical weakness is mob tarpits — War Horde Boyz locking a T8 Karnivore in melee and stripping it slowly, combined with the Cultist screen being too thin to absorb a full Ork advance, collapses the activation math that makes the list function.
471: Built around Knight Despoilers with paired Gatling Cannons alongside a Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos, this Iconoclast Fiefdom list uses its daemon-soup permission to bulk out screens and board control with Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, and Plaguebearers — Nurgle chaff that no pure Chaos Knights detachment can access. The engine is target isolation: Nurglings and Beasts clog midfield and deny deepstrike lanes while the Despoilers and Atrapos concentrate AP-3+ Melta and Gatling fire onto exposed priority targets, with War Dog Karnivores closing for melee cleanup. The Nurgle screen's T4-5 wound pools with FNP and the Knights' 4+ ion shield invulns mean concentrated anti-armour fire struggles to simultaneously crack the chassis and clear the board presence. Where it cracks is against Mass Volume Horde lists — 30-Boyz mobs and Beast Snagga Squighogs lock the Knights in melee through the activation gap, while the Nurgle chaff, despite its durability, lacks the damage output to punish the tarpit before primary scoring bleeds away.
472: Built around a Knight Tyrant and Knight Abominant anchoring a full Infernal Lance roster of TITANIC and super-heavy chassis — Cerastus Lancer for speed, Despoiler and Desecrator for ranged volume, Rampager for melee threat — this is an all-in big-knight list with almost no Wardog filler. The plan is to use 12"+ base movement and concentrated AP-3+ firepower (Tyrant's twin Gatling Cannons, Abominant's Warpstrike Claw) to isolate and delete priority targets each turn while the Lancer's superior speed contests mid-board secondaries the opponent can't reach. It punishes slow durable-grind lists — Death Guard Vectorium and similar T7-9 FNP-stacked armies can't out-trade focused Melta and paired Gatling fire across three or four TITANIC activations. The core weakness is activation count: with five or six models total, mobile-infantry lists and Mass Volume Horde builds simply outscores this list on primary while absorbing its firepower on cheap screening bodies, and any list packing dedicated anti-armour redundancy can focus the Tyrant off the table before its damage output pays back its points cost.
449: Built around Chaos Terminators with a Chaos Lord in Terminator Armour leading the hammer, supported by Obliterators as heavy fire-support anchors and Mutilators as secondary melee threats — this is a slow-grind terminator-brick list that doesn't fit cleanly into Pactbound Zealots' crit-engine or Soulforged Warpack's daemon-vehicle frame, instead leaning on raw Terminator durability and multi-role heavy weapon coverage from Havocs and Obliterators. The plan is to march the Terminator brick into midfield under Obliterator fire support, lock objectives with high-OC models, and win primary by being too expensive per model to efficiently remove. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists and skimmer kite builds that lack the concentrated AP-3+ or Melta volume to crack 2+ armor at volume — Havoc lascannons and Obliterator multi-melta flex cover both anti-tank and anti-elite roles. The 36% win rate exposes the core weakness: this brick is slow, predictable, and has no screen, so Transport Infantry lists with Rhino-rush Possessed and crit-stacking Pactbound Zealots, and Heavy Gunline Russ tanks with Demolisher blast templates, delete the Terminator delivery before it reaches the midfield objectives it needs to hold.
462: Built around Lord of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, and Be'lakor flanked by Screamers and Flamers, this is Shadow Legion running the full Tzeentch toolkit — mobile daemons with stacked invulnerable saves, Lethal Hits on Flamer volume, and Pink Horrors as a self-replenishing scoring core. The engine is Kairos's reroll-aura enabling Flamer mortal-wound fishing via Lethal Hits while Screamers slash across midfield objectives and Lords of Change generate Command Point pressure through Daemonic Ritual and deny counter-charges with 4+ invulnerable saves on every anchor unit. It punishes planted gunlines and transport-infantry lists badly — the Screamer speed and Be'lakor's -1-to-wound aura make this list nearly impossible to remove from objectives through standard AP-2 firepower, and Horror splits tax the opponent's kill efficiency every turn. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta and mobile anti-armour fire — Mont'ka Crisisuits or Knight Despoilers closing to 12" — crack the 4+ invuln stack faster than the Daemonic Ritual recursion can replace models, collapsing the scoring engine before the Flamers can return fire.
448: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane leading a Daemon Engine stable of Venomcrawlers, Defilers, and Forgefiends, backed by Warpsmith support and Cultist Mob screens, this is a Soulforged Warpack expression that leans into the vehicle-heavy end of the detachment's design space rather than the infantry-in-transports read. The plan is to use Vashtorr's Dark Pact and Warpsmith repair buffs to keep AP-3+ vehicle platforms firing at full efficiency while Cultists screen the backfield and Venomcrawlers close mid-board to lock key threats in melee, converting the daemon engine durability advantage into a primary-scoring stranglehold by turn three. It punishes planted gunlines and slow mid-range infantry through superior threat saturation — four to six distinct vehicle activations force opponents to split fire inefficiently, and no single loss collapses the engine because Warpsmith can restore wounds to the next platform in line. It struggles into high-speed mobile lists (Drukhari Raiders, Mont'ka Battlesuits) that can kite outside Dark Pact range and pick apart the Cultist screen with volume fire before the Venomcrawlers can close the gap.
443: Built around Deathwing Knights and the Lion himself anchoring a mixed terminator-and-infantry core, this is an Inner Circle Task Force trying to punch like a melee hammer while reaching across every other archetype without fully committing to any of them. The win condition is using Deathwing Knights' 2+/4++ and the Lion's Lethal Hits melee profile to grind the midfield while Gladiator Lancers provide AP-3 anti-tank reach and Jump Pack Intercessors contest secondaries — a multi-axis scoring plan that demands everything work simultaneously. It punishes slow, planted lists like AM Grizzled Company that can't reposition away from Deathwing charges or escape the Lancer's Laser Destroyer at range. The fatal crack is that 39% win rate reflects the core problem: the list is a generalist in a meta that rewards specialisation, the terminator delivery is expensive without a dedicated transport layer, and killing the Lion or the Chaplain Terminator collapses the buff chain holding the whole engine together.
437: Built around Plague Marines delivered in Chaos Rhinos, buffed by a Malignant Plaguecaster and Biologus Putrifier, with Poxwalker blobs holding ground and War Dog Brigand providing indirect-fire support, this is the Virulent Vectorium's sticky-objective grind list pushed toward a shooting-heavy configuration. The engine is simple: Rhinos deliver T5 Plague Marines onto midfield objectives where Disgustingly Resilient and Contagion debuffs make clearing them brutally inefficient, while the Biologus Putrifier stacks Lethal Hits on Blight Launchers to punish anything that tries to dig them out, and Poxwalkers absorb counter-charges on the flanks. Against mid-toughness infantry lists that rely on volume wounds to clear objectives, the FNP-equivalent layering and sticky-objective rule mean you simply never give up points even when you take casualties. The win rate signals a real problem: mobile anti-armour and fast skimmer lists exploit the complete absence of speed and heavy anti-tank, stripping the Rhinos turn one and leaving the Plague Marines walking into a trade they can't force at range or close fast enough to win in melee.
442: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Ravenwing Black Knights, and a Ravenwing Command Squad anchor, this is the Company of Hunters running a pure fast-vehicle pressure list — no boots on the ground, just a wall of skimmer chassis closing range at 14–16" per turn. The engine is speed-dictated firing position: Land Speeder Vengeances lay down Plasma Storm Batteries at mid-range while Black Knights and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes punch anti-armour holes via AP-3+ Melta and Assault-keyword shooting on the advance, scoring primary through sheer board coverage and objective denial rather than static holds. It punishes Heavy Gunline and Transport Infantry lists hardest — Russes and Rhino-rush armies can't match the movement or repositioning, and losing their transports on turn 1 to concentrated Melta and Plasma leaves CSM hammers walking into scoring deficits they can't recover from. The critical weakness is volume melee or dedicated anti-armour that matches its speed: Mid-T Brawler mobs tarpit the low-model-count chassis and grind hull points faster than the list can disengage, while Mobile Anti-Armour vehicles with equivalent movement and AP-3+ simply out-trade fragile speeder platforms that carry no meaningful invulnerable saves.
451: Built around Ravagers for long-range anti-armour, Kabalite Warriors in Venoms, Scourges with heavy weapons for fire support, and Mandrakes as an Archon-buffed melee/harassment piece, this is a Realspace Raiders-style Kabal gunline that leans heavier into static firepower than the canonical Reaper's Wager kite. The plan is to stack Dark Lance and heavy-weapon volume from Ravagers and Scourges into priority targets while Venoms advance-and-fire Splinter Cannon salvos into infantry, farming Pain Tokens to fuel the mid-game trade engine. It punishes slower durable lists — Death Guard Vectorium and planted gunlines can't reposition away from concentrated AP-2 Dark Lance fire, and Mandrake harassment from deepstrike denies backfield objective claim. The low win rate signals a core tension: too static to kite effectively and too fragile to plant, meaning any opponent with mobile anti-armour or a deepstrike melee threat can crack open the Ravager chassis before the Pain Token economy pays off.
436: Built around Deathshroud Terminators led by a Lord of Contagion, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, and Poxwalker screens, this is the Virulent Vectorium's elite-brick variant — a layered wall of T5-6 infantry and T7-8 vehicles grinding forward behind expendable bodies. The engine is attrition-through-stickiness: Vectorium's always-on sticky-objective rule locks scored primaries in place even as units die, while the Lord of Contagion delivers the Deathshroud into melee and the Bloat-Drones cycle Lethal Hits pressure from Contagion-debuffed flanks. It punishes Mid-T Mixed Brawlers and Mass Volume Hordes hardest — Poxwalker chaff absorbs the counter-charge while Blight-Hauler AP-2 volume and Deathshroud Manreapers with Lethal Hits chew through T5-6 bodies faster than Ork mobs can replenish. Mobile Anti-Armour is the crack: concentrated AP-3+ Melta from Knights or Mont'ka Battlesuits strips the Blight-Haulers and Bloat-Drones before the Deathshroud can close, and Disgustingly Resilient doesn't save T7 chassis from S8+ focused fire.
441:
Built around two Librarians — one on foot, one in Terminator armour — stacked alongside Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, and Sternguard Veterans delivered in transports, this is a Dark Angels Inner Circle Task Force leaning hard into the psychic-command-and-elite-melee identity of the Deathwing.

The engine is Librarian-buffed elite delivery: Companions and Deathwing Knights drop out of transports or deep strike into mid-board, amplified by psychic abilities that layer Lethal Hits or re-rolls onto already-hard-hitting 2+/4++ Terminator chassis, while Sternguard fire clears screens to open charge lanes and Scout squads claim secondaries on the edges.

It punishes slow durable-grind lists and planted gunlines that can't reposition — Terminator bricks with 2+/4++ shrug off static AP-2 fire and close the gap before a Heavy Gunline can kite, and the Sternguard's Special Issue Ammunition strips elite infantry that try to screen the charge.

The 41% win rate signals the core fragility: this build folds to mobile anti-armour and fast skimmer fire that pops the transports before the payload arrives — once Companions and Deathwing Knights are walking across open ground without the Librarian buff active, concentrated Melta or Dark Lance fire picks them apart faster than the 4++ can absorb.
450: Built around Lelith Hesperax leading Wyches and Incubi packed into Raiders and Venoms, with Reavers screening and Cronos Parasites providing Pain Token fuel, this is a Spectacle of Spite or Wych Cult shell running the full Drukhari close-combat toolkit. The plan is to advance the transport fleet turn 1, disgorge melee hammers onto isolated targets while Reavers grab secondaries, and cycle Pain Tokens through the Cronos to keep Wyches punching above their weight in sustained combats across turns 2 and 3. It punishes heavy gunlines and slow durable lists that can't kite — once Lelith and a full Wych blob make contact with a static shooting unit, the Bladestorm and extra attack volume deletes it before it can fall back into coherent firing arcs. Fast mobile anti-armour lists are the hard counter, as cracking the thin-hulled Raiders and Venoms with AP-3 Melta before the payload deploys collapses the entire delivery engine.
452: Built around Hellions, Succubus, and Wyches delivered in Raiders and Venoms, this is a Wych Cult-flavored Skysplinter Assault expression that plays more like a skimmer-horde hybrid than a pure kite list — Hellions' native 14" move and Fly keyword let them function as both objective-flood bodies and melee delivery, while the Succubus stacks Combat Drugs and Pain Tokens to spike their damage ceiling. The engine scores primary through sheer model volume: Hellions spread across mid-board objectives with high OC density while Scourges with heavy weapons punish anything that tries to clear them at range, and Wyches in Raiders threaten counter-charges against anything that commits to contesting. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation armies — the combination of 14"-move Hellion blobs and Venom-borne Wyches creates more contested objectives per turn than a Heavy Gunline Toolbox or Transport Infantry list can clear, especially when the Succubus is cycling Combat Drugs to generate melee threat across multiple angles. The list struggles against Mobile Anti-Armour opponents, specifically T'au Mont'ka or Chaos Knights Infernal Lance, whose AP-3+ concentrated fire can strip the Hellion model count fast enough to collapse the OC advantage before Pain Tokens reach critical mass.
465: Built around Daemonettes in mass, Fiends, a Keeper of Secrets, and a Defiler as the heavy backbone, this is a Slaanesh summoning-rush list running through Emperor's Children's Carnival of Excess or Court of the Phoenician frame — delivering daemon bodies forward via Chaos Spawn screening and Terminator anchor support. The engine is pure volume-over-objectives: flood midfield with Daemonette blobs carrying high attack counts and Locus of Swiftness charge-threat, use Fiends as fast flanking pieces to isolate scoring units, and let the Keeper of Secrets delete anything that contests a key marker. It punishes static gunlines and transport-mech armies brutally — the sheer activation count and T4 wound-pool overwhelms Russ firing efficiency and forces CSM-mirror opponents into unfavorable trades against a list that replaces losses through Daemon summoning. The vulnerability is concentrated high-AP anti-infantry fire with blast templates and Lethal Hits stacking — Plagueburst Crawler indirect or War Horde Sustained Hits 1 chews through unarmored T3 Daemonettes faster than the summoning engine can replenish them.
466:
Built around Noise Marines in Chaos Rhinos, Infractors as the melee anvil, a winged Daemon Prince of Slaanesh, and Lord Kakophonist stacking Sonic Weapon buffs, this is the Carnival of Excess transport-rush list — mid-range Slaaneshi aggression delivered by mech and punished into close combat.

The engine is disgorging Noise Marines and Infractors from Rhinos onto contested objectives while Kakophonist's aura stacks Sustained Hits 1 and the Daemon Prince hunts characters; scoring flows from objective control backed by the credible counter-charge threat these units generate once they dismount.

It punishes heavy gunlines and slow midfield-control lists that can't prevent the Rhino wave reaching objectives by turn 2, where the Sonic Weapon volume and Infractor melee output outgrinds anything that doesn't bring a durable enough counter-punch.

The list struggles when fast anti-armour or mobile shooting pops the Rhinos before they unload — losing the transports early exposes Noise Marines walking forward at 6", and without Kakophonist's aura fully online, the shooting output drops sharply enough that durable invuln-stacked or FNP-layered lists simply absorb the damage and out-score it.
464: Built around Infractors and Flawless Blades delivered in transports with a Lord Exultant driving the crit-stack, backed by Maulerfiend and Defiler daemon engines, this is Emperor's Children Pactbound Zealots or Soulforged Warpack running the Slaaneshi-melee-rush variant of the Rhino-push template. The engine is the Lord Exultant's Dark Pact crit amplification landing on Infractors mid-board — Devastating Wounds triggers on crits erase characters and elite infantry before they can answer — while Flawless Blades clear screening units and the Maulerfiend closes on vehicles the shooting can't finish. It punishes planted gunlines and low-activation anti-armour lists, where the combined threat saturation of transport-delivered melee plus two daemon-engine chassis forces impossible priority decisions across too few activations. It cracks open against dedicated heavy gunline opponents who pop the Rhinos turn one and against fast kiting lists where the slow-walk Defiler and Maulerfiend can't close the distance before the primary score gap becomes unrecoverable.
474: Built around Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight and multiple NDK chassis supported by Purifiers, Castellan Crowe, and Interceptors, this is a Sanctic Spearhead-style list that leans hard into the Mobile Toolbox pattern — fast invuln-stacked T6 walkers with teleport-strike delivery backed by elite infantry that can answer almost any threat profile. The engine is mid-board control through turn-1 teleport aggression: NDKs drop into threat range of the opponent's scoring units while Interceptors shunt across the table to contest secondary objectives, forcing reactive play that bleeds primary points. The 4+ invuln on every NDK chassis, Purifier Smite weight, and Brotherhood Librarian psychic support punish slow durable lists — Heavy Gunline Russ companies and Mass Volume Horde infantry blobs can't clear T6/4++ walkers efficiently before the score gap opens. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta from Mobile Anti-Armour lists and fast kiting from Drukhari skimmer fleets both stress this build hard, as NDKs become priority targets that Melta cracks reliably and skimmers simply outrange.
473: Built around Paladin Squads and Brotherhood Terminators led by Grand Master Voldus and a Brotherhood Chaplain, this is Hallowed Conclave at its most character-dense — a Terminator-armoured elite-infantry core with Interceptors providing mobility reach. The plan is to use Voldus's Psychic Fortitude and Chaplain litany buffs to push durable 2+/4++ Paladins and Terminators onto midfield objectives while Interceptors teleport-threaten secondaries and flanks, scoring primary through sustained presence rather than a single alpha-strike trade. Against Heavy Gunline Toolbox and static artillery lists it excels, because Teleport Shunt and Halcyon Warp Blessing let the army deny firing arcs and crash Terminator bricks into planted Russes before they can kite. It struggles into Transport Infantry and Mass Volume Horde matchups, where activation counts and raw body volume bury the limited model count under sustained scoring pressure — losing Voldus early collapses the buff chain that keeps Paladins punching through elite armor.
481: Built around a Knight Castellan fire-base supported by Knight Destriers, Errants, and a Crusader, this is a Questoris Companions-style combined-arms Imperial Knights list that mixes long-range deletion with melee threat across multiple chassis. The engine is concentrated AP-3+ and Melta fire — the Castellan's Plasma Decimators and Volcano Lance dictate target priority from turn 1, while Destrier screening and Errant/Gallant melee presence force the opponent to split attention between the ranged spike and the close-range threat closing on their flank. Ion Shield 4+ invuln across the roster plus Inquisitorial Agents utility gives the list genuine staying power against alpha-strike lists that can't reliably crack T10-12 chassis in a single activation, and the toolbox breadth means it answers both elite infantry and vehicle targets without hard list-building dependencies. The critical vulnerability is mob tarpitting — War Horde Orks or Mass Volume Horde AM blobs swamp the activation economy with bodies the Castellan's blast weapons can't efficiently clear before the mob locks the Knights in melee and the primary scoring race tips irreversibly to the opponent.
480: Built around two to four Armiger Helverins and Warglaives operating as a fast harassing screen backed by a Knight Warden or Paladin as the big-chassis anchor, with a Callidus Assassin providing precision character removal — this is the Skyreaper Lance expression of Imperial Knights, flooding activations with T8 Armigers rather than investing in a pair of Titanic Knights. The plan is to drown the opponent in mobile AP-3+ autocannon fire from the Helverins and Warglaive melee pressure simultaneously, contesting every objective with multiple 12"-move T8 bodies while the big Knight applies focused fire on whatever the Armigers have softened; the Callidus drops in to strip a key character buff and collapse an opponent's damage chain. The 4+ ion-shield invuln stacked across six-plus activations punishes anti-armour-light rosters — Mass Volume Horde and Transport Infantry lists that can't saturate enough AP-3+ into eight T8 wounds-each models fast enough to clear them before the Armigers score. The weakness is concentrated Melta or Knight-mirror fire: a Mobile Anti-Armour opponent with paired Gatling Despoilers or a T'au Mont'ka Riptide stack can focus down Armigers two-at-a-time before the activation advantage pays off, since each individual Armiger is far cheaper to erase than a Titanic chassis.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard delivered by Hekaton Land Fortress, backed by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn fire support and Hernkyn Pioneers racing the flanks, this is the Hearthband's attrition hammer — a Mid-T brawler that fights like War Horde crossed with a Russ gunline. The plan is to land the Hearthguard brick onto a priority objective turn 2, trigger their T5 2+ armor and Kin Sense rerolls to grind opposing elites off the board, while Thunderkyn Volkanite fire and Ironkin Steeljack heavy weapons suppress anything trying to dig them out at range. At 50% the list is exactly as advertised — it punishes slow durable grind lists and T4-5 infantry mobs that can't clear the Hearthguard brick before the primary scoring gap opens, but fast mobile lists that kite the Fortress or concentrate AP-3+ Melta onto the T9 transport crack the delivery engine before the hammer ever lands.
482: Built around paired Cerastus Knights — the Atrapos with its Atrapos Lascutter and Graviton Singularity Cannon cracking T9+ chassis, and the Lancer with its 14" movement and Shock Lance closing to melee range — anchored by Canis Rex as a durable character-led centrepiece and supported by Armiger Warglaives as fast screening harassment. This is a Skyreaper Lance-style mobile pressure list that wins by concentrating AP-3+ and Melta-equivalent firepower onto the opponent's key anti-tank or primary-scoring units in turns 1–2, using the Cerastus chassis's superior 14" move to dictate engagement range while Warglaives contest midfield objectives and deny deepstrike corridors. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Layered Lethal Combat lists hard — the Atrapos's Graviton Singularity Cannon cracks T9 vehicles that FNP-stacked Plague Marines or ion-shielded Knights rely on, and nothing in a Grizzled Company Russ line moves fast enough to reposition before the Lancers are already in their deployment zone. At roughly 50% it sits squarely in the middle of the meta, and the reason is activation count — against Transport Infantry or Mass Volume Horde lists the 5–6 activation ceiling means the Knights are constantly conceding primary on objectives they simply cannot contest in numbers.
432: Built around Sagitaurs delivering Hearthkyn Warriors and Ironkin Steeljacks into melee while Brôkhyr Thunderkyn and Arkanyst Evaluator-buffed fire bases hold the line, this is Leagues of Votann's Mercenary Oathband playing a hybrid War Horde game — armoured transports pushing mid-board while a planted heavy-weapon core covers their advance. The engine scores by flooding objectives with T5 Hearthkyn blobs backed by Sustained Hits volume from Thunderkyn, using the Brôkhyr Iron-Master to keep damaged Sagitaurs operational and extend the scoring window into turns 4-5. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists hard — Sagitaur speed (12" move) closes firing arcs before Heavy Gunline Toolbox can dictate the trade, and T5 bodies with layered Kin Bonds absorb the return fire that would fold lighter transports. It cracks against fast kiting lists and dedicated anti-infantry blast spam: Drukhari fire-and-fade denies the Sagitaur charge angles, and Demolisher-heavy Russ companies clear Hearthkyn squads faster than the Iron-Master can patch the vehicles back up.
456: Built around massed Necron Warriors with Canoptek Reanimators, Illuminor Szeras, and a Technomancer stack — this is Awakened Dynasty castle play, anchoring two large Warrior blobs behind a wall of resurrection tech while Immortals and Orikan the Diviner provide elite-tier board presence. The engine is attrition-by-numbers: Szeras's Technomantic Resurrection and the Reanimator's aura stack reanimation protocols to return 4-6 Warriors per turn, making the central objective blobs functionally unkillable while Immortals with Gauss Blasters contest flanks and score primary. It punishes gunlines and Transport Infantry builds that can't sustain the kill-rate needed to overcome stacking Reanimation — AP-1 and AP-2 shooting simply can't clear Warriors fast enough when two independent resurrection triggers fire every Command phase. Lists packing Melta, AP-3+ concentration, or melee that bypasses the Reanimation window (Fight on Death, Devastating Wounds) crack it open, as does anything fast enough to contest the flanks before the castle locks the center.
457: Built around Doomsday Arks as the long-range anti-armour spine, the Silent King as the commanding anchor, and Canoptek Scarab Swarms plus Flayed Ones providing the board-coverage screen, this is a Starshatter Arsenal castle with genuine mid-table teeth. The plan is to plant Doomsday Arks in a backfield fire position where their S14 AP-5 Doomsday Cannon can crack T9+ chassis at range, while the Silent King's aura buffs push Reanimation on surrounding units and Tomb Blades zip forward to contest midfield objectives and deny deep strike lanes. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count anti-armour lists that can't close the distance fast enough — the Scarab screen and Flayed Ones tarpit absorb alpha strikes while the Arks delete whatever the opponent invested their damage budget into. Where it cracks is against fast melee toolboxes and Transport Infantry rushes that can put bodies on objectives before the Scarab screen is established, outscoring the castle on primary while the Doomsday Cannons — built to delete vehicles, not clear 30-model mobs — waste activations on chaff.
486: Built around massive Boyz mobs led by Ghazghkull Thraka, Painboyz, and a dense stack of Warboss and Big Boss characters, this is War Horde at its most textbook — green tide volume fused with a punishing melee support network. The engine is pure OC domination: 30-Boyz blobs with Sustained Hits 1 from War Horde's detachment rule flood every objective turn one while Stormboyz deliver a flanking charge threat and Painboy FNP keeps the mobs alive long enough to outscore the opponent on primary. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Mobile Anti-Armour lists through sheer activation overload — a Russ company or Knight lance simply can't clear 60-90 wounds of T5 infantry fast enough to prevent the scoring flood. Fast kiting lists crack it open, since Drukhari Raiders and Aeldari Wave Serpents can park at 24" and chip Boyz off objectives all game without ever entering charge range.
431: Built around Cthonian Beserks delivered by Sagitaurs with Berehk Stornbröw and Buri Aegnirssen stacking their character buffs, this is a Mercenary Oathband-style melee-hammer list that brings a hard-hitting elite front line backed by Einhyr Hearthguard fire support. The engine is Berehk's charge-threat aura pushing T5 Beserks with Extra Attacks weapons into mid-board objectives while Sagitaur-mounted firepower strips light screening and the Hearthguard hold the backfield, converting sustained primary scoring into an insurmountable point lead by turn three. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists — Knights and Mont'ka T'au specifically — where Beserks lock chassis in melee through sheer T5 wound volume and the Sagitaur's mobility denies objective resets. Static shooting armies that crack Rhino-equivalent AV10 transports early unravel the delivery plan, and without the Sagitaurs keeping the Beserks alive to mid-board, the character-buff engine stalls before Berehk's melee spike can connect.
487: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Kill Rig, and a Beastboss on Squigosaur, this is Da Big Hunt at its most concentrated — a Beast Snagga-only roster with Mozrog Skragbad as the apex threat multiplier. The win condition is closing the distance fast with T5-6 bodies stacked behind Beastboss auras, getting the Kill Rig's psychic and melee output into the midfield by turn 2, and grinding primary through sheer wound-pool volume while Squighog Boyz punch well above their weight into T9+ chassis via Devastating Wounds. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour lists — Knights and Mont'ka in particular — where the activation gap and Beast Snagga charge-bonus delivery locks vehicles in melee before they can reposition. Fast kiting lists running high-AP Pistol or Assault fire at range are the hard counter, since the Beast Snagga engine collapses if it can't trigger the charge.
455: Built around Skorpekh Destroyers and Lords, Lokhust Destroyers and Heavy Destroyers, and Nekrosor Ammentar as the command anchor, this is Cursed Legion at its most focused — a Destroyer Cult list that weaponizes the detachment's chain-buff trigger to cycle S-bonus stacks across the entire roster. The engine is the kill-chain itself: when a Destroyer Cult unit destroys or halves an enemy unit, every non-Monster/Titanic Necron in the army gains +2 S that turn, making each successful trade geometrically more dangerous than the last, while Reanimation and 4+ invuln on key pieces keep the chain alive long enough to close games on primary. It punishes static heavy gunlines and slow grind lists hardest — the Lokhust Heavy Destroyers' AP-3+ anti-vehicle weight combined with Skorpekh melee pressure creates a two-axis threat that Russ companies and AM Grizzled Company can't cover simultaneously without ceding mid-board. The list cracks when Transport Infantry volume or Layered Lethal Combat defenses absorb the first kill-chain activation without breaking — Plague Marines behind Disgustingly Resilient or Pactbound Cultist screens eat the first trigger and leave the army's S-bonus cycling on empty for the rest of the turn.
469: Built around Terminator Assault Squads and Terminator Squads buffed by a Librarian in Terminator Armour and an Ancient, anchored by Redemptor Dreadnoughts and Intercessor backfield holders, this is the 1st Company Task Force expression of Codex Space Marines — a Terminator brick delivered on foot or via Land Raider with psychic and banner support stacking rerolls and durability layers. The engine is a mid-board Terminator wall that forces the opponent to trade into 2+/4++ models while Redemptors clear screens and Intercessors bank primary scoring, winning on attrition and sustained primary rather than a single kill spike. Against static Heavy Gunline lists, the 2+/4++ brick simply walks through AP-2 fire that can't shift T5 Terminators efficiently, and the Librarian's smite and buff suite keeps the hammer functional deep into the game. Against fast kiting lists — Drukhari Raiders and Aeldari Wave Serpents firing Assault-keyword weapons on the move — the Terminators' 5" base movement is a structural liability, as the opponent dictates range all game and the list lacks the speed or indirect fire to punish fire-and-fade repositioning.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan and Adrax Agatone riding inside a Land Raider Redeemer alongside Infernus Squads, this is a Firestorm Assault Force list that weaponizes the Salamanders' character stack to turn flame and melta profiles into a coordinated kill engine. Vulkan's aura stacking Lethal Hits onto Infernus and Eradicator weapons means every Sustained Hits 1 proc from the Redeemer's twin heavy flamers or the Infernus bolters generates additional mortal-wound triggers, while Eradicators provide the AP-3 melta punch for T9+ chassis. It punishes static gunlines and transport infantry hard — Blast-immune flamers ignore screening Cultists, and the Land Raider's T12 4+ invuln forces the opponent to dedicate concentrated anti-tank fire just to stop the delivery, buying Eradicators free angles on secondary targets. Mobile kiting lists are its ceiling — a Drukhari Raider or Wave Serpent that stays outside 12" Melta range and chips the Redeemer with Dark Lances can bleed the list down faster than the kill engine can disengage and re-approach.
488: Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, and Tankbustas backed by Mek support characters, this is an Ork shooting-specialist list that leans hard into the War Horde body-count framework while replacing the usual Boyz-and-Squighog melee engine with ranged dakka platforms. The plan is to flood mid-board objectives with a high-model-count screen — generating the Mass Volume Horde OC advantage — while Lootas and Flash Gitz grind down opposing units from the backfield and Tankbustas provide dedicated anti-vehicle punch against anything the Shokk Attack Gun's random-but-punishing S2D6 profile doesn't reach first. It punishes slower static armies that can't close the distance or reposition away from the Mek gunline's firing arcs, particularly Heavy Gunline Toolbox opponents who have no answer to an opponent willing to match their own planted-firepower game plan at a fraction of the points-per-body cost. However, it struggles badly into Skimmer Skirmish Fire lists that simply kite outside charge range indefinitely, and without the Sustained Hits 1 melee output of a proper War Horde, it can't brawl its way back into a game it's losing on primary — the sub-50% win rate reflects exactly this inability to close when the shooting stalls.
467: Built around Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts anchored by Marneus Calgar and Victrix Honour Guard, this is an Anvil Siege Force-style heavy gunline that uses the Repulsor chassis's 46"-range Macro Plasma Incinerators and the Ballistus's Twin Lascannon to plant sustained AP-2 and AP-3 fire across the board while Incursors and Scout Squads handle forward objective claim. The engine is simple: Calgar stacks rerolls onto the Repulsor Executioners, the Honour Guard keep him alive through dedicated wounds, and the shooting platforms delete priority targets each turn while Scouts deny deepstrike corridors and score Engage on All Fronts. It punishes low-invuln vehicle rosters and Transport Infantry lists hard — Rhinos and Land Raiders pop under sustained Lascannon and Macro Plasma volume before the cargo can deliver, and once transports are gone the CSM hammers walk into more shooting. Mobility-based lists that refuse the engagement, particularly Drukhari Reaper's Wager and Mont'ka JSJ Crisis Suits, crack it open by staying outside its firing arcs and chipping the expensive Repulsor chassis with anti-armour fire it cannot reposition to avoid.
477: Built around Repulsor Executioners as the fire-base spine, Blood Claws and Wolf Guard Headtakers as the close-quarters hammer, and Ragnar Blackmane leading Wolf Guard Terminators as the elite strike package, this is a Champions of Russ hybrid that tries to combine a rolling armoured gunline with delivered melee pressure. The plan is to use Repulsor Executioners' Heavy Onslaught Gatling Cannons to strip screens and force priority decisions while Ragnar's Terminators and Blood Claws close into charge range and score primary through attrition combat rather than clean gunline trading. It punishes lists that can't answer both vectors simultaneously — mid-T brawlers that ignore the Repulsors get shredded by S6 volume fire, while low-model-count anti-armour lists get swamped by Headtaker melee before they can focus the tanks. The split identity is also its undoing: dedicated heavy gunline armies like Grizzled Company out-trade the Repulsors at range before the melee wave arrives, and fast skimmer lists kite the slow T8 chassis while avoiding the charge entirely.
478: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry, Wulfen with Storm Shields, and Wolf Guard Terminators anchored by Bjorn the Fell-Handed, this is a Champions of Russ list that mixes durable elite melee with Scout-screened objective control — Wolf Jail in all but name, but without the mono-Thunderwolf commitment. The plan is to use Scouts and Intercessors to deny early charges and lock primaries while the Thunderwolf and Wulfen hammers punch into whatever the opponent exposes, leaning on Bjorn's Ancient Tactician aura to keep the activation economy competitive. It punishes static gunlines and transport-mech lists that can't clear T5 Storm Shield Wulfen efficiently before the cavalry arrive, and the mixed elite density means there's no single obvious kill-priority that collapses the engine. The weakness is its spread — no axis dominates above 7.4, so concentrated AP-2 or AP-3 volume from a Russ tank company or a Drukhari skimmer swarm finds the list's durability shallower than a true Wolf Jail brick and chips it apart before the melee can close.
479: Built around Grey Hunters in Impulsors, Venerable Dreadnoughts, and Wolf Scouts with Fenrisian Wolf screens, this is a Champions of Russ mid-range mech list that plays closer to a Rhino-rush Marine list than the Thunderwolf cavalry builds Space Wolves are better known for. The engine is Grey Hunter squads disembarking from Impulsors onto mid-board objectives turn 2, backed by Librarian buffs and Wolf Scouts denying deep-strike corridors, while the Venerable Dreadnoughts anchor the backfield and punish anything that tries to clear the screens. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists — the Impulsor's 14" move keeps the opponent's firing arcs honest, and Fenrisian Wolf screens eat the alpha strike that would otherwise gut the cargo. The multi-axis profile that makes it flexible is also its ceiling: without a dominant offensive spike — no Melta concentration, no Lethal Hits engine, no dedicated melee hammer — it struggles to close games against layered-defense lists like Virulent Vectorium or Custodes Talons that absorb the Grey Hunter trade without breaking.
428: Built around Riptide Battlesuits and Broadside Battlesuits as the heavy-fire backbone, supported by Piranhas and Stealth Suits for board control, this is a Mont'ka-style mobile gunline that marries AP-3+ anti-armour volume to a fast skirmish screen. The engine is Pathfinder-fed Markerlights unlocking full re-roll-to-hit on priority targets, letting Riptides and Broadsides delete a key chassis per turn while Piranhas and Stealth Suits deny forward objectives and screen the main battery from melee engagement. It punishes static heavy gunlines and slow durable lists — anything T7-9 that can't reposition eats focused Riptide Ion Accelerator or Heavy Rail Rifle fire before it can return the favour, and the Piranha skirmish layer stops melee threats from closing. The near-even win rate signals a list that is fundamentally honest but fragile to matchups that strip the Pathfinder support first or match its mobility, specifically fast anti-armour forces like Chaos Knights Infernal Lance that can close to Melta range before the firing solutions are established.
483: Built around Genestealers and a Broodlord, flanked by Lictors, Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, and Hormagaunt chaff, this is the Assimilation Swarm's infiltration-and-charge engine at its most committed. The win condition is layered threat saturation: Lictors and Raveners arrive from reserves to deny screens and create charge lanes while the Broodlord-buffed Genestealer blob closes on the primary objective, scoring through sheer OC and melee attrition once locked in. The 4+ invuln on Genestealers combined with Lictors' pre-game deep-strike denial and Ravener speed punishes Heavy Gunline lists that can't clear infiltrated threats before they're already in melee range. The build cracks open against Transport Infantry — a Cultist screen absorbs the first-wave charges, crit-stacked Pactbound shooting strips the Broodlord and collapses the synapse envelope before the swarm can sustain pressure into turns 3 and 4.
490: Built around multiple units of Tzaangor Enlightened delivering high-volume Disc-mounted shooting alongside Sekhetar Robots as a durable midfield anchor, supported by a Sorcerer and Tzaangor Shaman buff stack — this is Cult of Magic running the Tzeentchian beastmen engine rather than the traditional Rubric-heavy template. The win condition is layering Preternatural-Precision-equivalent Lethal Hits procs from the Enlightened's missile fire onto priority targets while the 4+ invuln Sekhetar Robots and Rubric Marines contest objectives and absorb return fire through their stacked defenses, out-scoring opponents on primary across turns three through five. It punishes static gunlines and mid-T brawler lists hardest — the Enlightened's mobility and range keeps them outside Russ firing arcs and Ork charge ranges, while Lethal Hits volume chews through T5-6 bodies faster than the mob can trade back. Fast anti-armour lists with concentrated AP-3+ Melta, particularly Mont'ka Crisis suits or Infernal Lance Knights, crack it open by threatening the Disc-mounted units before they can dictate range.
489: Built around Rubric Marines and Scarab Occult Terminators backed by a dense psyker staff of Sorcerers and Exalted Sorcerers, this is the Cult of Magic's attrition core — a mass-infantry shell that leans on Rubric volume, Tzaangor screening, and Terminator hammer units to contest every zone simultaneously. The engine scores by planting Rubric blobs across multiple objectives, exploiting their 4+ invulnerable save and All is Dust to absorb trading fire while Scarab Occults and character-buffed Fatecaster Enlightened generate AP-2 shooting pressure that chips away at whatever the opponent commits to clearing. It punishes static heavy gunlines and mid-table brawlers that expect to out-body it — the 4+ invuln across every Rubric model means blast templates and S5 volume fire underperform hard against this list's actual wound-per-point cost. The list cracks under concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour focus fire and fast melee threats that can isolate the character stack, since the entire damage engine degrades sharply if a Sorcerer or Exalted support piece gets precision-sniped before the psychic buffs land.
427: Built around Commander in Coldstar and Enforcer Battlesuits flanked by Crisis Sunforge, Fireknife, and Starscythe squads under Commander Farsight's aura, this is the Mont'ka Jump-Shoot-Jump engine at its most saturated — a pure battlesuit hammer with near-zero non-battlesuit models. The win condition is Melta and AP-3+ volume delivered via JSJ repositioning: Sunforges spike anti-armour on the forward commit, Fireknifes maintain mid-range pressure, and Farsight's Devastating Wounds trigger cleans up whatever survives while the Coldstar scouts secondary angles for Engage on All Fronts and Behind Enemy Lines. It punishes static gunlines and durable T7-9 chassis hard — concentrated Melta from multiple Crisis squads hitting on the move overwhelms Russ tanks and Marine heavy-weapon stations that can't reposition to break the JSJ cycle. Its critical weakness is activation-count attrition on objectives: a mob-heavy list or transport infantry swarm simply outnumbers the battlesuit roster in OC, and once the Crisis suits commit to a trade they can't screen every marker simultaneously.
429: Built around Kroot Carnivores and Krootox Rampagers screening for Breacher Teams riding Devilfish, this is the Auxiliary Cadre's mixed Kroot-and-pulse-rifle delivery list — a T'au take on the mass-infantry-plus-transport formula that floods mid-board with cheap bodies while Devilfish-mounted Breachers threaten objective-to-objective repositioning. The win condition is drowning the opponent in OC from Carnivore blobs and Krootox Riders while Breachers disembark point-blank for their S5 AP-1 pulse blaster burst, with the Cadre Fireblade's reroll-1s-to-hit Order keeping the Breacher spike reliable. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour lists and planted gunlines that can't clear the Kroot screen fast enough before Breachers arrive, leveraging the activation-count gap that 10-plus small units create against 4-6 vehicle opponents. However, any list running blast templates or high-volume Lethal Hits — Grizzled Company Demolishers, Aspect Host Dark Reapers, War Horde Sustained Hits 1 — clears the Carnivore chaff before it can threaten objectives, and the Breachers' 5" range means they die in the transport if the Devilfish gets popped early.
485: Built around Exocrines, Tyrannofexes, and Maleceptors alongside a Norn Emissary and Screamer-Killers anchored by a Hive Tyrant, this is Crusher Stampede's signature monster-density roster — durable T9-10 chassis with 4+ invulnerable saves stacked across nearly every activation slot. It wins by flooding mid-board with high-toughness bodies that contest objectives while the Exocrine and Tyrannofex fire bases pour out sustained S9-10 AP-2/AP-3 shooting that punishes anything that tries to dig them out at range. Static gunlines and volume-infantry builds fold fastest here — blast-immune T9+ monsters with FNP-equivalent durability simply absorb the firepower that normally clears objectives, and the sheer OC density makes primary scoring nearly automatic against lists that can't clear multi-wound models efficiently. The crack is concentrated AP-3+ Melta or mobile anti-armour pressure — a Knights or Mont'ka list that can close within Melta range and focus-fire individual monsters one per turn will grind through the roster faster than the Synaptic Imperative buffs can compensate, since there's no real screen and no deepstrike denial to slow the approach.
491: Built around Forgefiends and Defilers anchored by Exalted Sorcerers on Discs and a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, this is a Warpforged Cabal expression that leans hard into daemon-engine fire support backed by Sekhetar Robots and Tzaangor Enlightened arcing shots from elevation. The engine is straightforward: Forgefiend Hades Autocannons and Defiler Battle Cannons (Blast, AP-2, range 48") pour concentrated anti-elite and anti-horde fire downfield while the Disc Sorcerer and Daemon Prince deliver Tzeentch psychic buffs that stack Lethal Hits and 4+ invuln across the daemon-engine chassis, creating the heavyGunline and layeredLethal overlap the data flags. It punishes slow midfield lists — Mass Volume Horde infantry blobs and Mid-T Brawler Ork mobs — where Defiler Battle Cannon Blast templates and Forgefiend volume fire clear bodies faster than the opponent can replace OC, while the Daemon Prince's 4+ invuln and flying threat range keep screens honest. Fast anti-armour pressure (Knights, Mont'ka Crisis Suits) cracks it open, as concentrated AP-3+ Melta deletes T9 daemon engines before the Disc Sorcerer's invuln buffs can offset the damage per activation.
484: Built around the Norn Assimilator as a T10 melee-murder engine, supported by Psychophage, Haruspex, and Pyrovores as a dense mid-board monster wave, this is an Assimilation Swarm list that floods the table with regenerating biomass and smashes into objectives rather than shooting across them. The win condition is the Synaptic control game collapsed into pure board presence: Ripper Swarms claim and sticky objectives cheaply while the monster wave grinds through whatever is contesting them, with the Norn Assimilator's Devastating Wounds melee profile and the Psychophage's mortal-wound aura doing the heavy lifting on elite clearing. It punishes Transport Infantry and Mid-T Brawler lists that try to engage the monster wave directly, because T9-10 chassis with FNP-stacked support simply absorb the return damage and keep generating bodies from Ripper Swarm reinforcement. It cracks apart against Mobile Anti-Armour — concentrated AP-3+ Melta and Knight-speed repositioning can isolate and delete the Norn Assimilator before the monster wave closes distance, stranding the cheaper screening units without their anchor.
495: Built around Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, Slaughterbound, and Khorne Berzerkers in Chaos Rhinos, this is the Berzerker Warband in its purest competitive form — a Khorne-mark stack across diverse melee profiles, with Chaos Spawn as cheap screening bodies that trigger Fight on Death via Mark of Khorne. The engine is maneuver-then-engage: Rhino delivery parks Berzerkers onto mid-board objectives by turn 2 while Eightbound and Slaughterbound teleport or advance into isolated targets, scoring primary through 4+ invuln bodies that are genuinely hard to shift in a single shooting phase. It punishes static Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists brutally — once Eightbound are in melee with Russes, the tanks can't fall back without surrendering the trade, and Apoplectic Frenzy turns a single activation into a board-clearing spike. The 40% win rate tells the real story: Devastating Wounds shooting from Transport Infantry lists eats the Spawn screen and kills characters before the melee engine connects, and any list packing AP-3+ Melta volume can crack the T6 Eightbound chassis before it reaches combat range.
496: Built around Skarbrand, a Lord on Juggernaut, and a core of Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, and Bloodcrushers backed by Forgefiend fire support, this is a Goretrack Onslaught-style Khorne daemon-tide running inside a World Eaters shell — fast T4-5 bodies with 4+ invuln on the Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds, Lethal Hits baked into Skarbrand's melee profile, and a Forgefiend providing the anti-armour arc the daemon units can't cover. The win condition is a coordinated turn-2 charge wall: Flesh Hounds screen-clear on the advance, Bloodcrushers lock priority targets in melee where the AP-2 Hellblade volume and Skarbrand's Lethal Hits attacks grind through 3+ armor, while the Forgefiend's Hades Autocannons punish anything that tries to fall back or reposition. Against mid-toughness brawler lists and Heavy Gunline tanks it excels — Bloodcrushers at T5 with a 4+ invuln absorb Russ fire efficiently and the model count overwhelms activation-starved vehicle rosters on objectives. Fast anti-armour lists running concentrated AP-3+ Melta (Mont'ka Crisis suits, Infernal Lance Knights) crack it open by targeting the Forgefiend early and then kiting the daemon melee wave without ever entering charge
